answer: Little in the provided evidence speaks against the requirement. Feedback and the US study consistently show vents and touchscreen-only controls are hard to find and distracting, so the user need is strong. The only limiting points are the stated uncertainties: some customers prefer full-touch solutions and HMI changes may force center-stack repackaging. These raise feasibility and segmentation risks but do not negate the need.
suggested_change: Relax the strict 90%/5s pass threshold to 85% or allow separate thresholds by solution type; require usability trials to include touchscreen-preferring participants and accept physical controls, haptic shortcuts, or UX improvements that meet the adjusted criterion.
